modules.title: Transactions and Concurrency
modules.goal: Make multi-step changes atomic and reason about isolation and locks.

topics.title: Transaction Basics
topics.simple: Transaction multiple statements ko ek unit banata hai.
topics.pro: A transaction groups statements so they commit together or roll back together.
points: It ends with COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

topics.title: BEGIN
topics.simple: BEGIN transaction start karta hai.
topics.pro: BEGIN starts an explicit transaction block and disables autocommit until the block ends.
points: It can be implicit in some clients.

example.sql: BEGIN;

topics.title: COMMIT
topics.simple: COMMIT changes ko permanent karta hai.
topics.pro: COMMIT makes the transaction’s changes visible and durable, then ends the block.

topics.title: ROLLBACK
topics.simple: ROLLBACK changes ko undo karta hai.
topics.pro: ROLLBACK discards all changes in the transaction and releases its locks.
points: It cannot undo a committed transaction.

topics.title: ACID
topics.simple: ACID atomicity, consistency, isolation aur durability deta hai.
topics.pro: ACID describes atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability, the guarantees that make transactions trustworthy.

topics.title: Isolation Levels
topics.simple: Isolation level concurrent transactions ke visibility rules set karta hai.
topics.pro: PostgreSQL supports Read Committed, Repeatable Read and Serializable, each trading concurrency for stronger guarantees.

example.sql: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ;

topics.title: Read Committed
topics.simple: Read Committed har statement ko naya snapshot deta hai.
topics.pro: Read Committed sees data committed before each statement starts, so the same query can see different rows within one transaction.

topics.title: Repeatable Read
topics.simple: Repeatable Read transaction ke snapshot ko stable rakhta hai.
topics.pro: Repeatable Read uses one snapshot for the whole transaction, preventing non-repeatable reads but allowing serialization failures on write conflicts.
points: Writes can fail with serialization errors.

topics.title: Serializable
topics.simple: Serializable strongest isolation deta hai.
topics.pro: Serializable makes concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one at a time, aborting when a serialization conflict is detected.

topics.title: Dirty Read
topics.simple: Dirty read uncommitted data dikhata hai.
topics.pro: A dirty read sees another transaction’s uncommitted changes; PostgreSQL does not allow it at any isolation level.

example.output: The other session sees the old value.

topics.title: Non-repeatable Read
topics.simple: Non-repeatable read same row ko do baar different dikhata hai.
topics.pro: A non-repeatable read occurs when a row changes between two reads in the same transaction; Read Committed allows it, Repeatable Read prevents it.

example.output: Both reads see the same snapshot.

topics.title: Phantom Read
topics.simple: Phantom read naye rows ko dobara query me dikhata hai.
topics.pro: A phantom read occurs when a re-run query sees new rows that match the predicate; stronger isolation prevents it.

topics.title: Row Locks
topics.simple: Row locks competing updates ko serialize karte hain.
topics.pro: UPDATE and DELETE take row-level locks that block conflicting writes until the transaction ends.

example.output: The row is locked until commit.

topics.title: SELECT FOR UPDATE
topics.simple: SELECT FOR UPDATE rows ko lock karta hai.
topics.pro: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks selected rows so another transaction cannot change them before you do.

topics.title: Deadlocks
topics.simple: Deadlock do transactions ke circular lock wait se hota hai.
topics.pro: A deadlock occurs when transactions wait on each other’s locks; PostgreSQL detects it and aborts one transaction.

topics.title: Savepoints
topics.simple: Savepoint partial rollback allow karta hai.
topics.pro: SAVEPOINT marks a point inside a transaction; ROLLBACK TO undoes work after it without ending the whole block.

topics.title: Autocommit
topics.simple: Autocommit har statement ko apna transaction banata hai.
topics.pro: With autocommit on, each statement commits immediately; an explicit BEGIN groups statements until COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

topics.title: Long Transactions
topics.simple: Long transactions locks aur vacuum ko rok sakte hain.
topics.pro: Long-running transactions hold locks, retain snapshots and delay vacuum cleanup, so keep them short.

example.sql: SELECT pid, state, xact_start FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE xact_start IS NOT NULL;

topics.title: Common Transaction Errors
topics.simple: Missing COMMIT, wrong isolation aur deadlock retries common errors hain.
topics.pro: Common failures are forgetting to commit, assuming ROLLBACK works after commit, and not retrying serialization or deadlock failures.
points: Do not hold locks during UI waits.

topics.title: Practical Transaction Pattern
topics.simple: Begin, validate, modify, verify, commit ya rollback.
topics.pro: A safe write transaction previews the target, performs the change, verifies affected rows and commits only when the result is correct.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Transaction Basics in a production query.
interview.answer: A transaction groups statements so they commit together or roll back together. Key rules: All-or-nothing. It protects multi-step changes. It ends with COMMIT or ROLLBACK.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain BEGIN in a production query.
interview.answer: BEGIN starts an explicit transaction block and disables autocommit until the block ends. Key rules: It starts the unit. It can be implicit in some clients. Nested BEGIN warns.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain COMMIT in a production query.
interview.answer: COMMIT makes the transaction’s changes visible and durable, then ends the block. Key rules: It makes changes permanent. It releases locks. It cannot be undone afterward.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain ROLLBACK in a production query.
interview.answer: ROLLBACK discards all changes in the transaction and releases its locks. Key rules: It undoes the block. It works after errors. It cannot undo a committed transaction.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain ACID in a production query.
interview.answer: ACID describes atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability, the guarantees that make transactions trustworthy. Key rules: Atomic: all or nothing. Consistent: rules hold. Isolated: concurrent work is controlled. Durable: committed data survives.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Isolation Levels in a production query.
interview.answer: PostgreSQL supports Read Committed, Repeatable Read and Serializable, each trading concurrency for stronger guarantees. Key rules: Read Committed is the default. Repeatable Read is snapshot-based. Serializable can abort transactions.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Read Committed in a production query.
interview.answer: Read Committed sees data committed before each statement starts, so the same query can see different rows within one transaction. Key rules: Default level. Statement-level snapshot. Non-repeatable reads are possible.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Repeatable Read in a production query.
interview.answer: Repeatable Read uses one snapshot for the whole transaction, preventing non-repeatable reads but allowing serialization failures on write conflicts. Key rules: Stable snapshot. No non-repeatable reads. Writes can fail with serialization errors.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Serializable in a production query.
interview.answer: Serializable makes concurrent transactions behave as if they ran one at a time, aborting when a serialization conflict is detected. Key rules: Strongest guarantee. Retries are required. It can reduce concurrency.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Dirty Read in a production query.
interview.answer: A dirty read sees another transaction’s uncommitted changes; PostgreSQL does not allow it at any isolation level. Key rules: Uncommitted data. Not possible in PostgreSQL. It would break atomicity.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Non-repeatable Read in a production query.
interview.answer: A non-repeatable read occurs when a row changes between two reads in the same transaction; Read Committed allows it, Repeatable Read prevents it. Key rules: Same row, different value. Read Committed allows it. Repeatable Read blocks it.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Phantom Read in a production query.
interview.answer: A phantom read occurs when a re-run query sees new rows that match the predicate; stronger isolation prevents it. Key rules: New matching rows. Repeatable Read prevents most cases. Serializable prevents anomalies.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Row Locks in a production query.
interview.answer: UPDATE and DELETE take row-level locks that block conflicting writes until the transaction ends. Key rules: Locks are held to commit. Readers usually do not block. Long transactions hold locks longer.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain SELECT FOR UPDATE in a production query.
interview.answer: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE locks selected rows so another transaction cannot change them before you do. Key rules: Use inside a transaction. It blocks competing writers. It can deadlock.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Deadlocks in a production query.
interview.answer: A deadlock occurs when transactions wait on each other’s locks; PostgreSQL detects it and aborts one transaction. Key rules: Avoid inconsistent lock order. Keep transactions short. Retry the aborted transaction.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Savepoints in a production query.
interview.answer: SAVEPOINT marks a point inside a transaction; ROLLBACK TO undoes work after it without ending the whole block. Key rules: Create with SAVEPOINT. Roll back to the name. Release when done.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Autocommit in a production query.
interview.answer: With autocommit on, each statement commits immediately; an explicit BEGIN groups statements until COMMIT or ROLLBACK. Key rules: Default in many clients. BEGIN disables it temporarily. Multi-step work needs a block.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Long Transactions in a production query.
interview.answer: Long-running transactions hold locks, retain snapshots and delay vacuum cleanup, so keep them short. Key rules: Short blocks are safer. Avoid user think-time. Monitor pg_stat_activity.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Common Transaction Errors in a production query.
interview.answer: Common failures are forgetting to commit, assuming ROLLBACK works after commit, and not retrying serialization or deadlock failures. Key rules: End every block. Retry transient failures. Do not hold locks during UI waits.

interview.q: Module 19 · Explain Practical Transaction Pattern in a production query.
interview.answer: A safe write transaction previews the target, performs the change, verifies affected rows and commits only when the result is correct. Key rules: Preview first. Check the row count. Commit or roll back explicitly. Handle retries.

debug.title: Missing COMMIT
debug.broken:
BEGIN;
UPDATE students SET marks = 90 WHERE id = 1;
debug.error: The change stays uncommitted and locks are held

debug.title: Rollback after commit
debug.error: ROLLBACK has nothing to undo after COMMIT

debug.title: Savepoint typo
Deadlock order
debug.fix: Use one consistent order in every transaction, such as id 1 then id 2.

debug.title: FOR UPDATE outside block
debug.broken: SELECT * FROM students WHERE id = 1 FOR UPDATE;
debug.error: The row lock is released immediately without a transaction

debug.title: Serialization failure
debug.fix: Retry the whole transaction after a serialization failure.
debug.error: could not serialize access due to concurrent update

debug.title: Truncate lock
debug.error: TRUNCATE takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock

debug.title: Long transaction
debug.fix: Keep the transaction open only around the database work.
debug.error: Locks and snapshots are held during the wait

debug.title: Function COMMIT
debug.broken: CREATE FUNCTION f() RETURNS void AS $$ BEGIN COMMIT; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
debug.fix: Use a procedure for transaction control, or remove COMMIT from the function.
debug.error: COMMIT is not allowed in a function

debug.title: Isolation after query
debug.error: SET TRANSACTION must be called before any query
